messages:
maria: Ran an nsys trace on the nightly KV-heavy Llama2-7B seq512 workload — seeing a big shift in kernel time distribution. Attaching the top kernels I pulled. Anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:
kevin: which commit/regression did you bisect to? :thinking_face: did this start after the batcher prefix-merge change?
maria: looks correlated with the batching heuristic change on 2026-03-16 (batcher: prefer-prefix-merge). Host-side logs show many more short batches (avg tokens/batch down ~22%). Suspect launch overhead and small-KV writes.
perfbot: nsys summary snippet from the trace Maria uploaded:
```
nsys statistics report - sample
Total GPU active time: 14.82s
Top kernels by GPU time:
  masked_attention_forward        6.21s   41.9%
  kv_cache_write                  2.90s   19.6%
  dgrad_collapse                  1.45s    9.8%
  fused_fill                      0.77s    5.2%
  softmax_fused                   0.59s    4.0%
(others <3%)
```
jasdeep: masked_attention_forward with that % often means many small launches or low occupancy. On A100 if SM util <40% it's launch/warp-setup dominated. Can you attach a perfetto flame?
oliver: can you also paste the kernel launch counts? Launch count + avg duration tells the story (many short kernels vs fewer long ones). I ran a quick rank on a similar trace earlier:
```
rank  kernel                      pct_time  calls   avg_ms
1     masked_attention_forward   41.9%     1420    4.37ms
2     kv_cache_write             19.6%      890    3.25ms
3     dgrad_collapse              9.8%      310    4.67ms
4     fused_fill                  5.2%      120    6.42ms
5     softmax_fused               4.0%       78    7.56ms
```
kevin: hypothesis: the prefix-merge heuristic reduces token coalescing so we get many small KV write kernels; kernel launch overhead accumulates. Two levers: increase coalesce window OR aggregate KV writes on CPU into bigger batches.
maria: quick experiment: bumped `batcher.window_ms` in the dev config from 4 -> 12 (local test). Re-ran trace with same workload, results below.
```
after change: Total GPU active time: 12.12s
Top kernels:
  masked_attention_forward   3.41s  28.1%
  kv_cache_write             1.37s  11.3%
  dgrad_collapse             1.32s  10.9%
  fused_fill                 0.77s   6.3%
  softmax_fused              0.70s   5.8%
```
jasdeep: nice — that supports the coalescing hypothesis. SM util moved from ~27% -> ~37% in the profile, so fewer launches and higher work per launch. Still suboptimal but much improved.
kevin: can we make the batching change behind a feature flag and run canaries across other models (codegen, chatty small models) to ensure no regression where latency spike matters? Also add an automatic detector: if `masked_attention_forward` > 35% of GPU time suggest increasing `batcher.window_ms` or enabling `kv_agg=true`.
oliver: I'll update the kernel-priority map used by runtime to prefer `masked_attention_forward` friendly kernels when avg_launch_duration < 8ms. Also add a small script to compute top-10 kernel % from nsys CSV and push to the perf dashboard.
maria: command I used to repro the trace: `nsys profile -o out_nv --trace=cuda,nvtx ./run_inference --model llama2-7b --seq-len 512 --batch 8`. Full trace uploaded to s3://redwood-nightly/trace/2418001234/.
perfbot: perf alert: masked_attention_forward median latency increased 1.9x vs baseline on nightly. Alert id: perf-2418-03.
jasdeep: I'll add a console metric: per-kernel GPU-time percentage (sampled at 5m) and a rule: if any single kernel > 35% for >10m trigger perf-signal. That should catch regressions without relying on model-specific thresholds.
maria: filing a small PR to: 1) put batching.window behind flag, 2) add the perf check in the console, 3) add playbook notes for triage (include sample `nsys` commands and the kernel-ranking script). Linking in PR in a bit. Thanks all :pray:
kevin: thanks — once PR lands let's run the nightly smoke matrix and watch the perf dashboard for 24h. If green, we can flip the flag.
oliver: also add the perf traces to nightly artifacts and pin the before/after nsys CSVs to the incident page.
maria: will do. uploading final traces and opening the PR now.
